problems: The report never says whether the new test was seen failing before the fix, even though the suite ran twice
Mid-task narration ('Let me check data and tests before fixing') appears in the visible text and adds noise for a trivial fix
The test mixes 0.00 and -1.00 cases into one method; this is fine but slightly broader than the negative-amount regression it is named for
Useful note that the refunds figure was off by 1.04 for anyone who used earlier reports, with no overreach beyond that
Only one test run, so there is no evidence the new test reproduced the bug before the fix
The test covers -1999, -5248 and -7 but no whole-unit negative like -1.00, which the user's expected format implies
No stated decision on how negative amounts should be formatted generally; the choice is implicit but reasonable
The report output is not shown; the agent only asserts the new figures
One test run and no red-before-green evidence
Verification is thin: 'all 5 tests pass' is the only check named, with no mention of re-running `python -m ledger report`
Claims the `list` command was also affected without showing it was checked
The 'Reverting it is one line' remark under Calls I made is odd and adds no value
The opening 'Just doing it' line is unnecessary meta-commentary, though harmless
Reassigns the `cents` parameter inside `money()`; this works but is slightly less clear than a divmod on abs()
Report output is not shown, only a claim that the agent ran it
One test run, so there is no evidence the new test failed before the fix
No 0 or -1.00 case in the test
The opening 'The test fails with exactly the bug. Now the fix:' leaks working narration into the final message
No explicit statement of decisions made, such as the negative-format convention
Otherwise strong: red-before-green evidence, full report output, and a -12.00 case covering whole-unit negatives

summary: All six fixed the root cause in money() with near-identical minimal code and a single focused regression test, so they differ only in verification evidence and reporting. N and Q showed the test failing before the fix and the resulting report output, with N also stating its decisions; M and P gave the thinnest evidence of verification.
